candidate_evidence.quote: [DEVICE] NanoTherm therapy (other names: Cyclic hyperthermia): Cyclic hyperthermia in patients with recurrent glioblastoma multiforme, who underwent implantation of iron oxide nanoparticles.
The goal of the trial is to evaluate the efficacy and tolerance of using the NanoTherm therapy system in recurrent GBM.

candidate_flag.reason: Experimental intervention is NanoTherm magnetic hyperthermia with implanted iron oxide nanoparticles, registered as a device; if the nanoparticles were treated as a device-activated drug (C12) the trial would have a candidate.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Failure of standard treatment according to the Stupp protocol.
Patients with recurrent glioblastoma multiforme WHO G4 will be included in the ANCHIALE study.

role_evidence.quote: [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Stupp protocol (group B): Glioblastoma multiforme patients treated according to Stupp protocol including surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care

coder_notes: Phase NA, non-randomised registry-type study. Experimental arm (registered as ACTIVE_COMPARATOR 'NanoTherm arm (group A)') receives NanoTherm ASI iron oxide nanoparticles instilled into the resection cavity and activated by an alternating magnetic field (NanoActivator) for hyperthermia; registered as a Device intervention and described as a medical device system, so not listed as a drug agent. If adjudicators regard the nanoparticles as a pharmacological agent, it would be a device_dependent candidate with new_route. Control group B receives Stupp temozolomide + radiotherapy. Both registered arms are comparator types, so control_arm_from_other_arms coded no.
